name: Tiefentalalm
beschreibung:
Overview

The Tiefentalalm is an alpine hut at 1,880 metres above sea level amid the mountains of the Kaunergrat, high above the Pitztal valley. It lies within the municipality of St. Leonhard im Pitztal in the district of Imst and is run by the Neururer family. The hut is a traditional place to stop for refreshments, reachable above all on foot via hiking trails. When you stop here you can enjoy traditional Tyrolean specialities, hearty snacks, sweet alpine dishes and chilled drinks. From its location the view extends to the Rofelewand and the Gsallkopf. Situated directly on the Gschwandbach stream, a large sun terrace invites you to linger. The hut is a popular destination for hikers and offers a quiet atmosphere in unspoilt nature.

History/Background

A documented founding or ownership history of the hut is not recorded in the available official sources; reliable historical information therefore cannot be substantiated. What is verified is that it is run as a family business by the Neururer family. The hut is open only in the summer months and then goes into winter dormancy. According to the operator and the Pitztal tourist board, the Tiefentalalm is currently closed and will not reopen until summer 2027.

Getting there

The Tiefentalalm cannot be reached by car; access is exclusively on foot. The ascent begins in the Scheibe district at the Gasthof zur Einkehr at 1,382 metres above sea level. From there you cross the bridge and follow the well-built farm track or a trail uphill. For the roughly 498 metres of elevation gain to the hut at 1,880 metres, you should allow about 1.5 to 2 hours of walking time. The hike to the Tiefentalalm described in the sources also starts in Scheibe.

Tips

For families there is a playground in the immediate vicinity of the hut. On request, an overnight stay at the hut is possible: a cosy room has four double beds for a maximum of eight people, bedding is provided and breakfast is included; electricity and showers are not available. As the hut is currently closed, it cannot be reached by phone – contact is possible by email. Anyone planning to stop here should check the current opening situation in advance.

Best time to visit

The Tiefentalalm is open only in the summer months. The rest of the time it is in winter dormancy. Currently the hut is closed and, according to the operator and the tourist board, will not reopen until summer 2027.
